Retrieve a registered engine

Source: R/engine-registry.R
get_lsa_engine.Rd

get_lsa_engine() returns the registry entry of one engine: its name, its function, its description and the packages it requires. It is the lookup lsa() performs before fitting, and it is useful for inspecting a built-in engine's function or for checking that a registered engine can run in the current session. To see which engines exist, use list_lsa_engines().

Usage

get_lsa_engine(name)

Arguments

name

Name of the engine.

Value

A list with the elements name, fn, description and requires, as given to register_lsa_engine().

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and one of:

  • lagdynamics_unknown_engine: no engine is registered under name.

  • lagdynamics_missing_package: a package the engine requires is not installed.

See also

list_lsa_engines(), register_lsa_engine()

Examples

str(get_lsa_engine("classical"), give.attr = FALSE)
#> List of 4
#>  $ name       : chr "classical"
#>  $ fn         :function (transitions, structural_zeros = NULL, alternative = c("two.sided", 
#>     "greater", "less"), n_events = NULL, ...)  
#>  $ description: chr "Bakeman & Quera classical lag sequential analysis"
#>  $ requires   : chr(0)
